title: Siemens Healthineers signs Letter of Intent with Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
summary: To advance capacity building and training for Egyptian radiographers

Siemens Healthineers, a leading global medical technology company, signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs during the second edition of the Terminal Europe Labour Mobility Forum 2026 in Cairo. Image Courtesy: Siemens Healthineers

To advance capacity building and training for Egyptian radiographers

Press Release

  • The Letter of Intent was signed at the second edition of the Terminal Europe Labour Mobility Forum 2026 in Cairo.
  • The initiative brought together the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Health and Population, GIZ and Siemens Healthineers to strengthen the technical and clinical capabilities of Egyptian radiographers.
  • Through specialized CT and MRI training, the program strengthened radiographers’ ability to effectively use advanced imaging technologies, supporting high-quality clinical practice and better patient outcomes.

Cairo, Egypt, Siemens Healthineers, a leading global medical technology company, signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) with Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs during the second edition of the Terminal Europe Labour Mobility Forum 2026 in Cairo. The LoI was signed by Amro Kandil, Managing Director of Siemens Healthineers Egypt, and Ambassador Nabil Habashi, Egypt’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, in the presence of Ambassador Jürgen Schulz, German Ambassador to Egypt; Ambassador Angelina Eichhorst, Head of the European Union Delegation to Egypt; Prof. Dr. Mohamed Fawzi, Minister of Health Advisor for Radiology Affairs and Supervisor of General Radiology Department at the Ministry of Health; and representatives from Egyptian ministries and embassies. The signing reinforced the partners’ shared commitment to developing the skills and capabilities of Egyptian healthcare professionals and strengthening the healthcare workforce.

The initiative formed part of the broader cooperation between Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, in partnership with the Ministry of Health and Population. The Ministry of Health and Population supported the participation of Egyptian radiographers in the program, GIZ contributed its expertise in international cooperation and skills development, while Siemens Healthineers brought its specialized expertise in medical imaging and technical and clinical training in computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Together, the partners combined public-sector leadership, healthcare workforce development, international cooperation and medical technology expertise to strengthen local capabilities and create greater value for Egypt’s healthcare system and its patients.

The program focused on strengthening radiographers’ technical and clinical capabilities and supporting the effective use of advanced medical imaging technologies. By developing their CT and MRI skills, the initiative aimed to support higher-quality clinical practice and ultimately contribute to better patient outcomes. It also supported the radiographers’ professional development and enhanced their readiness for employment opportunities in Egypt and internationally.

The forum also featured a high-level panel discussion titled “Towards a European Approach to Labour Mobility Partnerships with Egypt,” bringing together representatives from Egyptian ministries, the EU Delegation to Egypt, the German Embassy and European partners. The discussion explored ways to strengthen Egypt-Europe cooperation on fair and sustainable labour mobility, focusing on skills development, qualifications recognition, institutional coordination and preparation for employment opportunities in Europe.

The event also celebrated the 47 Egyptian radiographers who completed the first phase of the initiative in September 2026. Participants received specialized technical and clinical training in CT and MRI, strengthening their understanding of advanced imaging technologies and their ability to use them effectively in clinical practice. By building these capabilities, the program supports greater accuracy and quality in imaging, helping healthcare professionals make better-informed clinical decisions and ultimately contributing to improved patient outcomes.

Commenting on the signing, Amro Kandil, Managing Director of Siemens Healthineers Egypt, said: “Building a skilled healthcare workforce is essential to strengthening healthcare systems and ensuring that advanced medical technologies deliver their full potential for patients. Through this initiative, we invested in the technical and clinical capabilities of Egyptian radiographers, strengthening their ability to work effectively with advanced imaging technologies while supporting their professional development. The first phase demonstrates the value of partnerships that bring together public-sector leadership, international cooperation and technical expertise to build sustainable healthcare capabilities.”

The initiative reflects Siemens Healthineers’ broader commitment to advancing healthcare education and strengthening local expertise through practical training, simulation-based learning and collaboration with healthcare institutions and public-sector partners. This commitment was also demonstrated through the Ismailia Simulator Laboratory, developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Health to provide simulation-based training that equips healthcare professionals to work with advanced medical technologies.

Siemens Healthineers is also working to expand the scope of the Siemens Healthineers Academy into the Middle East and Africa Healthcare Education Center (MEA HEC), with the ambition of extending access to specialized healthcare education and professional development opportunities across the region. Through these initiatives, Siemens Healthineers continues to invest in local expertise, strengthen healthcare capabilities and support the development of a skilled and sustainable healthcare workforce.

About Siemens Healthineers

Siemens Healthineers pioneers breakthroughs in healthcare. For everyone. Everywhere. Sustainably. The company is a global provider of healthcare equipment, solutions and services, with activities in more than 180 countries and direct representation in more than 70. The group comprises Siemens Healthineers AG, listed as SHL in Frankfurt, Germany, and its subsidiaries.

As a leading medical technology company, Siemens Healthineers is committed to improving access to healthcare for underserved communities worldwide and is striving to overcome the most threatening diseases. The company is principally active in the areas of imaging, diagnostics, cancer care and minimally invasive therapies, augmented by digital technology and artificial intelligence.

In fiscal 2024, which ended on September 30, 2024, Siemens Healthineers had approximately 72,000 employees worldwide and generated revenue of around €22.4 billion.

Further information is available at www.siemens-healthineers.com.
